mainEntity.name: Do you provide rehabilitation clinic cleaning in Medford, MA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Medford (Middlesex County) is one of the 109 Massachusetts cities and towns we serve. It is about 23 miles east of our Marlborough base in a straight line. Every engagement starts with a free on-site assessment; call (978) 307-8107.

mainEntity.name: Which Medford ZIP codes do you cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: All of them: 02153, 02155. If your facility sits on a town line, tell us the street address and we will confirm.

mainEntity.name: Which nearby towns do you also serve?

acceptedAnswer.text: The closest served towns to Medford are Somerville (about 2.3 mi), Malden (about 2.6 mi), Winchester (about 2.7 mi). See the full list on our service areas page.

mainEntity.name: We store clean and just-used equipment on the same rack. Is that a real finding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. CDC Core Practices 5f expects physical separation between clean and soiled items, so that a cleaned item cannot be recontaminated or mistaken for a used one. In a busy gym the workable version is a designated soiled bin or drop zone for anything a patient has handled, a separate clean shelf, and a convention everyone follows without thinking. We can supply and service that routing, but the layout decision is yours. It costs almost nothing to fix and it is among the first things an assessor looks at.

mainEntity.name: Can you clean and maintain our whirlpool or hydrotherapy tank?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Tank filling, draining, chemical treatment, and disinfection are clinical equipment protocols set by the tank manufacturer, with their own logs and competency requirements, and they belong to your staff. We clean the room around it: floors, drains, walls, benches, handrails, and door hardware, which is where wet-area soil actually accumulates. If the hydrotherapy area shows standing water, a slow drain, or degraded flooring, that goes into our report, because those are environmental conditions and raising them is our job.

mainEntity.name: How do I know your crew knows what it is doing in a clinical gym?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because training and competency validation are documented rather than assumed. Section I item B of the CDC Infection Prevention Checklist expects cleaning personnel to receive job-specific training and competency validation at hire and whenever procedures or products change. Our crews are trained on clean-to-dirty sequencing, color-coded microfiber, contact time discipline, and the specific products in your building, with records kept per person. Jeneva Thomas founded Dory's after 22 years of clinical experience, which is why the training is written around real findings rather than around a supply catalog.

Rehabilitation Clinic Cleaning for Medford facilities

For rehabilitation clinics in Medford, the risk we plan around is direct skin contact with shared equipment all day, with no barrier — MRSA and fungal transfer. The surfaces that decide the outcome: treatment tables, mats, therabands, free weights, exercise balls, parallel bars, treadmills.

  • Speech Therapy
  • Sports Medicine

What inspectors cite — and how we prevent it

Real, published regulatory findings — every citation links to its source.

CDC Infection Prevention Checklist for Outpatient Settings, Section I Environmental Cleaning item A

No written policies and procedures for routine cleaning and disinfection of the gym, treatment tables and shared equipment, including who is responsible for what.

CDC Infection Prevention Checklist for Outpatient Settings, Section I item D

Cleaning is never monitored or assessed — no evidence the clinic checks that it is consistently and correctly performed.

Treatment tables, mats, weights and bands that contact intact skin are wiped but not cleaned and then disinfected between patients at the level the degree of soiling requires.

How we clean rehabilitation clinics in Medford

Where contamination concentrates

  • Treadmill and bike handles and consoles
  • Parallel bars and balance equipment
  • Therapy balls and foam rollers
  • Check-in counter
  • Door handles
  • Light switches

What the crew does, in order

  1. Agree which equipment staff wipe between patients and which the cleaning crew handles at end of day.
  2. Clean and disinfect treatment tables and mats with products compatible with vinyl and upholstery.
  3. Wipe down weights, bars and cardio equipment handles and consoles.
  4. Keep gym cloths separate from restroom cloths.
  5. Log areas completed and any damaged equipment surfaces we notice.

How often

  • Treatment tables and shared equipment: between patients by staff, full clean daily.
  • Restrooms and changing areas: daily or more often.
  • Waiting room: daily.

Rehabilitation clinics are typically cleaned after the last appointment, since the gym is in use all day.

Documentation you receive

  • Gym and treatment-room checklist
  • Product list with EPA registration numbers and contact times
  • Safety Data Sheets
  • Signed service logs

Questions worth asking at the walkthrough

  • Which products will you use on our table upholstery and mats?
  • Will you clean the free weights and cardio equipment every visit?
  • What will our staff still need to wipe between patients?

We answer each of these in writing after the free assessment.
